summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: Article 27 of the UN Charter (the codified institutional kernel) read by the P5 nations as a necessary structural safeguard preventing direct great-power war (a coordination Rope) versus read by the Global South as an extractive, un-amendable mechanism entrenching a permanent geopolitical oligopoly (a Snare). The exact same textual rule emits entirely different classifications depending on the observer's power and exit options.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The UDHR (the foundational normative kernel) read by international tribunals as establishing universal, binding, and actionable individual rights that supersede state boundaries versus read by sovereign states as a purely aspirational, non-binding framework subordinate to domestic jurisdiction. The contest centers on the text's authority grounding and its capacity to coerce state actors[cite: 2, 3].

summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The statutory debt ceiling (the fixed legal kernel) read originally as a procedural coordination mechanism to facilitate treasury borrowing without repeated congressional votes (a Scaffold) versus read in modern contexts as a hard, weaponized boundary allowing legislative factions to extract political concessions under the threat of sovereign default. An institutional rule heavily subject to interpretive drift[cite: 2, 3].

human_readable: UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)
summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The UNCLOS framework (the shared treaty kernel) read via strict geographic definitions regarding natural features and Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) versus read expansively to assert that artificial island construction generates sovereign territorial waters. The competing readings determine the boundaries of maritime resource extraction and military navigation[cite: 2, 3].
